title: Interleaved Head Attention
claim: Mixing heads into interleaved pseudo-tokens lets standard sliding-window causal attention capture cross-head interactions at modest cost.
layout: 1 panel, left-to-right, color-coded stacks feed a zoomed attention matrix
description: A single wide left-to-right diagram. At the far left, three gray query vectors (q1, qh, qH) are stacked diagonally. A green arrow labeled 'Linear transform ×α_Q' leads to a grid of pink, blue and orange tilted bars, which are the pseudo-tokens. Each head has P of them. Double-headed arrows mark 'Heads (H)' in green and 'Pseudo tokens (P)' in red. Dashed lines zoom into an 'Interleaving' step. The Q̃ column is a stack of repeating pink, blue and orange blocks, outlined in red. On the right, a K̃ row and a Ṽ column use the same colors. Between them is a teal softmax and causal-mask matrix with diagonal bands for the sliding window (N/2P). × symbols connect Q̃, K̃ and Ṽ. A legend sits at the bottom, and a sequence-length arrow (P·N) runs along Ṽ.
caption: Overview of Interleaved Head Attention (IHA). First, the model generates $P$ pseudo-tokens for each of the $H$ original heads via a learned linear transformation ($\times \mathbf{\mathcal{\alpha}_Q}$) operating on the heads axis (green). These tokens are then interleaved to create an expanded sequence of length $P \cdot N$. Finally, standard causal self-attention is computed on this expanded sequence, utilizing a sliding window (e.g., $N/2P$) to manage computational complexity while enabling cross-head interaction. Different linear transforms are used in query, key and values.
abstract: Multi-Head Attention (MHA) is the core computational primitive underlying modern Large Language Models (LLMs). However, MHA suffers from a fundamental linear scaling limitation: $H$ attention heads produce exactly $H$ independent attention matrices, with no communication between heads during attention computation. This becomes problematic for multi-step reasoning, where correct answers depend on aggregating evidence from multiple parts of the context and composing latent token-to-token relations over a chain of intermediate inferences. To address this, we propose Interleaved Head Attention (IHA), which enables cross-head mixing by constructing $P$ pseudo-heads per head (typically $P=H$), where each pseudo query/key/value is a learned linear combination of all $H$ original queries, keys and values respectively. Interactions between pseudo-query and pseudo-key heads induce up to $P^2$ attention patterns per head with modest parameter overhead $\mathcal{O}(H^2P)$. We provide theory showing improved efficiency in terms of number of parameters on the synthetic Polynomial task (IHA uses $Î(\sqrt{k}n^2)$ parameters vs. $Î(kn^2)$ for MHA) and on the synthetic order-sensitive CPM-3 task (IHA uses $\lceil\sqrt{N_{\max}}\rceil$ heads vs. $N_{\max}$ for MHA). On real-world benchmarks, IHA improves Multi-Key retrieval on RULER by 10-20% (4k-16k) and, after fine-tuning for reasoning on OpenThoughts, improves GSM8K by 5.8% and MATH-500 by 2.8% (Majority Vote) over full attention.
